faq.q: What does a product URL (the page address) give you?
faq.a: If the page opens with no login, you get its main image, the product name and any reviews on that page.

faq.q: Does the product link write the script?
faq.a: Yes. A script is written from the page, and you can edit the lines, the captions and the language before the clip is finished.
No. Plans start at $24.50 a month. Credits are what that plan spends on each video. A clip uses 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. You see that number before you start.

faq.q: How do I make a video from a product link?
faq.a: Paste the page address. Pick an actor and a voice, then check the script. Choose a size and a length. Then download it, or post it on TikTok, Facebook or Instagram.

faq.q: Can I use a public Shopify or Amazon page?
faq.a: Yes, if the page opens with no login and shows the item you sell, such as that color or size.

faq.q: What if the page requires a login?
faq.a: Upload the product photo directly. A locked page cannot be read.

faq.q: Can reviews on the page appear in the clip?
faq.a: Yes. When the page has reviews, they can be brought into the script so the clip mentions what buyers already said.

faq.q: How many credits does a URL to video clip use?
faq.a: A clip uses 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. Credits are what your plan spends. If the video fails, those credits come back.
A tall phone video is 9:16. A square is 1:1. A wide video is 16:9. 4:3 is a little wider than square. 3:4 is tall, but 9:16 is taller.

faq.q: Can I make clips for several product links at once?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the links you want and make a clip for each one, instead of rebuilding every ad by hand.

faq.q: Can I edit the script, the voice and the captions?
faq.a: Yes. Change the script, swap the voice, fix a caption and pick a song in the editor before you download or post.

faq.q: How long do I wait for a clip from a product page?
faq.a: You confirm the actor, the script and how many credits it uses. The clip is then ready to download. The 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds is how long the video is, not how long you wait. If it fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Can I publish to TikTok, Facebook or Instagram?
faq.a: Yes. Send the finished clip to TikTok, Facebook or Instagram from the same screen, or download it. You can use it in paid ads and in posts you publish yourself. No logo is stamped on the file. Check each app's rules before you spend more on ads.

faq.q: Is a person in the clip a real customer?
faq.a: No. Any person on screen is made by AI. They are not a real customer who bought the product.

reviews.h2: How Shops Turn a Product Link Into an Ad
reviews.lead: How ten kinds of sellers start from one public listing. These are examples, not quotes.

items.d: A store seller pastes a public listing, checks the photo and the script, and shows one action of the product.
A gadget seller uses the stand's public page, picks an actor, and asks for one unfolding action so shoppers can see how it opens.
A store running ads takes the same listing, makes one paid post about a single point, and publishes it on Facebook or Instagram.
A social seller pastes the listing again, picks a tall 9:16 size, and posts it to TikTok, Instagram or YouTube Shorts.
A beauty shop lets the page's reviews into the script so the clip mentions what buyers already noticed.
A catalog seller pastes a handful of product links and makes one clip for each item in that sitting.
A wellness seller keeps the same product page and makes a second clip in another language for a new market.
A home shop picks an actor and a voice, then edits one line of the script before downloading.
A small team trims the clip, fixes a caption and swaps the music in the editor. Then they download a file with no logo stamped on it.
A drink seller sends the finished clip to TikTok from the same screen after checking how many credits it will use.
